Note:

European expansion: back, leg, toe
Oceania expansion: back, ear, foot, head, mouth, wattle
Asia: brow, nape, vent, wattle
  • The Azure Tit, Willow Tit, and White-Browed Tit-Warbler do not qualify for the Anatomist card: in this case, "tit" comes from an Old English word meaning "small thing."

Americas expansion: brow, ear, foot, head, leg, nape, tuft, wattle

rulings.text: The Anatomist bonus card was reprinted in the Asia expansion with 6 points instead of 7 for 4+ birds. The change was unintentional, but the most recent version of the card is the official one.

Only the keywords listed on the card and in the relevant sections of the expansion rulebooks qualify a bird. Substrings that coincide with body-part names do not count when they do not refer to a body part (e.g., the wing in Burrowing Owl).

Both "beak" and "head" are on the Anatomist list, so birds such as Blue Grosbeak and Loggerhead Shrike count. "Horn" is not on the list, so Horned Lark does not count; follow the printed list strictly, including the additions in the expansion rulebooks.
Back is a body part for this bonus card, as listed in the European Expansion rulebook ("Anatomist (birds with body parts in their names): back, leg, toe"), so Canvasback counts toward it.
Desert Wheatear counts toward the Anatomist bonus card ("ear").
On this bonus card "name" refers only to the common name, not the scientific name.

A single bird may count toward more than one bonus card. These bonus cards never look at scientific (Latin) names, and other language editions handle them differently, so check the rulebook of the edition you are playing.

Words that refer to a body part only figuratively do not count: the "poll" in Blackpoll Warbler and the "start" in redstart names are interpretations of a word rather than anatomical words. A group may agree to count them, as long as it is consistent.

Note:
Count the number of birds that have the maximum possible number of eggs on them, according to their egg limit.

Note: Count the birds you played that have a face value of 0, 1, 2, or 3 points.

rulings.text: For Behaviorist, a column is a straight stack of card slots within a single row position across the three habitats. The birds with 3 different power colors must all be in the same column; colors matched diagonally or in other arrangements do not count.

Note: Count the birds you played that have the specific symbol shown on this bonus card. The symbol should be on the left-hand side of the bird’s brown power.

Red Junglefowl counts toward the Cartographer bonus card, since "jungle" appears in its name.

The only keywords that qualify a bird to count toward this bonus card are those listed thereon, including prairie (which is printed on this bonus card only in newer printings), and those in the relevant sections of the expansion rulebooks.

Birds in your habitat with the fewest birds.
Explanatory text: Ties count.
Note: Count the number of birds you played, in the habitat where you played the fewest birds. If you have two habitats tied for fewest birds, you may still score this bonus. For example, if all of your habitats have 3 birds in them, your habitat with the fewest birds has 3 birds in it.

rulings.text: Score only one habitat for the Ecologist bonus card, even if two or three habitats are tied for the fewest birds; the maximum score is therefore 10 points.
A habitat with no birds counts as your habitat with the fewest birds (0 birds), so an empty habitat scores 0 points.

Hummingbird cards are birds and count toward bonus cards in the ordinary way, including Bird Bander, Ecologist, Ethologist, Passerine Specialist, Small Clutch Specialist, and the Data Analyst and Ranger bonus cards.

Bird powers only take effect once the bird has been played, so Western Yellow Wagtail does not count double for Visionary Leader if you leave it in your hand. For Ecologist, counting it twice does raise the number of birds in its habitat, so if the habitats otherwise hold equal numbers of birds, its habitat is no longer the one with the fewest.

Note:

Explanatory text: Birds with no power count as white.

rulings.text: At the end of the game, choose one habitat (row), ignore the other two, and score 2 points for each distinct power color present in that row (including white/no power), not 2 points per bird. Multiple birds of the same color score that color only once, so 4 brown and 1 white bird score 4 points; the maximum is 8 points, from at least 4 birds of 4 different colors in one row.
Hummingbird cards are birds and count toward bonus cards in the ordinary way, including Ethologist.

rulings.text: Food Web Expert counts only birds whose food cost is [invertebrate] and nothing else. A bird with any other food symbol in its cost, even as an alternative, counts for 0. The appendix reads: "Count the number of birds that have [invertebrate] in their food cost and no other symbols."

Condition: Consecutive birds in [forest] with ascending or descending wingspans
VP: 3 consecutive birds: 3[point]; 4 consecutive birds: 5[point]; 5 consecutive birds: 8[point]
Note:
These bonus cards each grant points for a long enough sequence, in the corresponding habitat, of consecutive birds with wingspans in ascending or descending order. The sequence need not consist of all birds in the habitat, and it need not start or end with the first or last bird in the habitat. A sequence may include two or more birds with the same wingspan.

As mentioned earlier, the wingspans of flightless birds are wild: For purposes of these bonus cards, you can assign a flightless bird any wingspan.

For example, if the wingspans of the first 3 birds in your wetland are in ascending order, but the fourth bird in your wetland has a wingspan smaller than the third bird there, the length of your sequence is 3, in which case the Wetland Data Analyst bonus card would grant 3 points.

rulings.text: This bonus card only awards points for a single sequence of bird cards of increasing or decreasing wingspan.

Condition: Different nest types in [forest]
Explanatory text: You may count each star nest as any other type or as a fifth type.
Note:
For the birds that you played into the habitat specified on this card, count how many different nest types you have.
You may Count each star nest as any other type or as a fifth type. For example, a bowl nest, a platform nest, and three star nests can count as 5 different nests.
Birds with no nest do not count as having a nest type.

Condition: Consecutive birds in [forest] with ascending or descending scores
Explanatory text: Each bird's score must be higher than the next. You can go right to left or left to right.
VP: 3 consecutive birds: 3[point]; 4 consecutive birds: 5[point]; 5 consecutive birds: 8[point]
Note:
Within the specified habitat, these bonus cards each grant points for a sequence of birds that is in ascending or descending order by their point value.
  • The birds in the sequence must be in a continuous line on the board. The sequence need not consist of all birds in the habitat, and it need not start or end with the first or last bird in the habitat.
  • Numbers need not be consecutive, as long as they are ascending or descending.

rulings.text: The Ranger bonus cards use strict ascending/descending, so repeated point values break the series (unlike Data Analyst, which explicitly allows equal wingspans). With scores of 6, 5, 5, 4, 3 in [forest], Forest Ranger scores only the longest strictly ascending or descending series: 5, 4, 3.

Tied scores do not count as ascending or descending - 5 is not higher than 5 - so scores of 1-2-2-3-5 in [forest] count as a sequence of three, not five, and a run of 5, 5, 3, 3, 3 forms no sequence at all.

Note: Count the number of birds you played that only have the habitat symbol shown on this bonus card. If a bird has the option to live in more than one type of habitat, it cannot count toward this bonus.

Condition: Point value of your [mango] token
Sets of the 4 nest types
Explanatory text: Each star nest can be treated as any 1 nest type. No card can be part of more than one set.
Note:
This card is looking for sets of the four nest types among all of your birds. The order and location of the nests do not matter; it only matters that each set includes all four nest types.
Each star nest can be substituted for one nest of any type in one set. For example:
  • a cavity nest, a platform nest, and two stars would be a complete set.
  • two cavity nests, two platform nests, a bowl nest, a ground nest, and two stars would be two complete sets.
  • two bowl nests, two cavity nests, two platform nests, and one star nest count as one set, not two, because the star nest can only be a member of one set.

rulings.text: A bonus card with tiered scoring awards only the amount for the tier reached, not points per qualifying bird. On Cartographer you must have at least 2 qualifying birds to score 3 points and at least 4 to score 7 points.
Only one scoring category on a bonus card is scored: score either for 1 set of the 4 nest types or for 2 or more sets, not both.
